faqs.a:
The traffic engineer, or his designee, is hereby authorized to issue parking permits
               in accordance with the provisions of this article to allow the on-street parking of
               motor vehicles by residents of any block designated by the traffic engineer as a restricted
               parking area adjacent to an affected public school or as a restricted parking area
               adjacent to an affected public park. Parking permits shall be, at all times, the property
               of the city. Loss or theft of said permits shall be reported immediately to the traffic
               engineer.
(1)
It shall be unlawful for any person to sell, for money or other thing of value, a
                  parking permit issued by the traffic engineer.
(2)
The traffic engineer shall have the authority to deny, suspend, or revoke any parking
                  permit when he determines that the applicant, or any person holding a permit issued
                  to the applicant's address, has violated the provisions of this article. When the
                  engineer determines that a provision of this article has been violated and that a
                  permit shall be denied, suspended or revoked, the procedure shall be as follows:
a.
The applicant or permit holder shall be notified, in writing, by certified mail, addressed
                  to the applicant's or permit holder's address of record with the traffic division,
                  at least seven days prior to the denial, suspension or revocation.
b.
Upon receipt of the notice, the applicant or permit holder may request a hearing.
                  Such a request shall be made in writing to the traffic engineer within 14 days of
                  the receipt of the notice.
c.
If the written hearing request is timely filed, the traffic engineer shall set a time,
                  date and place of the hearing and so notify the applicant or permit holder.
d.
The traffic engineer shall conduct the hearing. The applicant or permit holder and
                  other interested parties may be in attendance and give testimony or present evidence
                  at the hearing. The traffic engineer shall notify the applicant or permit holder of
                  his findings and ruling in writing by certified mail within 14 days after the completion
                  of the hearing.
e.
The applicant or permit holder may appeal an adverse decision of the traffic engineer
                  to the city manager by filing a written request for appeal to the city manager within
                  14 days of receipt of the ruling of the traffic engineer. Upon receipt of the request
                  for appeal, the city manager, or his designee, shall review the record and render
                  a final written decision within a reasonable period of time. The city manager shall
                  notify the applicant or permit holder of his decision by certified mail.
(3)
The administrative remedies set forth in this article may be pursued notwithstanding
                  the commencement of any criminal prosecution alleging a violation of this article
                  or the lack of such criminal prosecution. All such administrative remedies are independent
                  of and shall be in addition to any penalties and powers of the city as set forth in
                  this Code.
(Code 1981, § 17-126; Ord. No. 2804, § 1, 4-15-1991; Ord. No. 2996, § 1, 8-16-1993;
               Ord. No. 3435, § 1, 2-2-1998;
Ord. No. 4561, § 2, 8-29-2016
